reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents technical chart commentary on DOT and frames the approximately $3.05 target as a personal expectation contingent on a breakout, not a guaranteed outcome. It includes a disclaimer that the material is not financial or investment advice and warns that cryptocurrency investments are high-risk and may result in losing most or all invested funds. The request to subscribe is ordinary audience engagement.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the price projection alongside the viewer-facing invitation. The speaker gives an upside target, saying it is where he expects the price to reach if a breakout occurs. The description then invites viewers to join a crypto school to improve their investing skills. Those are not the same as an explicit instruction to buy DOT, but together they can steer a viewer from an appealing appreciation scenario toward a linked investing offering. The conditional language narrows the prediction; it does not erase that promotional connection.

Nor does the absence of guaranteed profit settle whether an appreciation forecast is being used to attract viewers to an external offering.

A careful judge should weigh that sales context, not only the cautionary wording.
